toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
This looks like a single chance QC outlier on Analyzer B, not a real fault. The repeat on the same vial passed. The other two QC levels and sodium and chloride were normal. QC means are unchanged since the new reagent lot. Patient medians are stable. Re-testing 43 samples on Analyzer A agreed with Analyzer B within 0.02 mmol/L on average. QC ran on time for every scheduled slot, so the skipped-QC suspicion isn't supported. One flag in a month is about what you'd expect by chance. I can't tell whether it was a sampling glitch or chance, so don't record a cause as confirmed.

Ward 6's high potassiums are split evenly between Analyzers A and B. They coincide with the tube outage, which means long transport delays. Most of the high results had delays over 3 h. Renal overflow patients are another possible explanation. I haven't proven the delays are the cause.

Sign off: return Analyzer B to potassium service and close the 186-result review with no amendments. Don't recall results, quarantine the lot, or widen the limits. Consider extra Level 2 QC for a week. Ask Ward 6 for repeat samples and expedite the tube repair. I'm fairly confident, and I collected no extra evidence.
